title: Move the search query onto placeholders
summary: Turn a concatenated SELECT into a prepared statement and allowlist the sort order.

files.content:
<?php

final class UserRepository
{
    public function __construct(private readonly PDO $pdo)
    {
    }

    public function search(string $name, string $order): array
    {
        $sql = "SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%" . $name . "%' ORDER BY created_at " . $order;

        return $this->pdo->query($sql)->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
    }
}

turns.user: review says sql injection in UserRepository::search. can you sort it out

assistant.body: Dropping the concatenation for a placeholder and prepare. The LIKE wildcards move off the SQL and onto the bound value, so a name cannot smuggle one in.

turns.user: $order is still glued straight on. and a name with % in it still matches everything right

assistant.body: Both fair. A sort direction cannot be bound, so it goes through an allowlist instead. The % and _ in the name get escaped, with an ESCAPE clause to back it.

turns.user: changed my mind, newest first should be the default. empty order means DESC

assistant.body: Flipping the ternary so DESC is what you fall back to. An empty or unknown order now sorts newest first, and only a literal ASC climbs.
